messages:
Maya (PM): Quick sync — we've got a couple of enterprise customers asking for stronger tenant isolation + clearer pricing bands. want a proposal by EOW for prioritization.
Leo (Arch): Can we define isolation as discrete tiers rather than per-tenant bespoke configs? e.g. 'bronze/silver/gold' isolation surfaces: network, compute pool, KV cache sharing.
Sam (Eng): Agree tiers make sense for roadmap. Implementation-wise: bronze=shared pools + best-effort affinity; silver=dedicated slices with soft-eviction; gold=isolated pool + no noisy-neighbor batching.
Anne (SRE): Need to call out failover semantics. For silver, we allow cross-slice fallback during capacity pressure; for gold we never fall back automatically. That will affect SLA commitments.
Rick (Sales): Customers want both: predictable latency and data isolation. They asked about pricing delta for gold vs silver — need ballpark %s to justify.
Maya (PM): Action: Leo + Sam draft tech proposal + cost impact. Anne to write SLO matrix + rollback criteria. Rick to gather customer willingness-to-pay examples.
Leo (Arch): Two big tradeoffs: operational cost (more pools) and capacity efficiency (lower utilization). Also cross-region routing complexity if gold tenants are pinned to regions.
Sam (Eng): Implementation note: we can reuse existing routing policy layer, add a 'tenancy_tier' attribute to routing decisions. Quick pseudocode:
```yaml
routes:
  - match: tenant_id in gold_list
    route: dedicated_pool:us-west-1-gold
    policy: no_fallback
  - match: tenant_region: eu
    route: regional_affinity
```
Maya (PM): Nice. Include an opt-in path + migration experience levels (self-serve, SE-assisted, full-migration) in the plan.
Anne (SRE): Rollout proposal: pilot with 2 non-critical gold tenants for 6 weeks. Success metrics: p99 latency under target, <1% request fallback, incident rate change <= baseline. Rollback if metrics degrade >10%.
Rick (Sales): We need launch criteria phrased for contracts: "Gold SLA: 99.95% uptime, p99 latency < 250ms, data residency in EU/US as requested". Is that realistic?
Leo (Arch): 99.95% is a tight SLA for gold (requires replication + cross-region failover). If we pin gold to single-region, SLA should be slightly lower unless we commit to multi-region active-active.
Sam (Eng): Option: define two gold flavors: gold-local (single-region, lower cost) vs gold-ha (multi-region active-active, premium). That maps to sales asks neatly.
Maya (PM): Good call. Add pricing buckets: bronze (base), silver (+20%), gold-local (+60%), gold-ha (+150%). These are placeholders — finance will refine.
Anne (SRE): Operational playbook items: eviction soft-timers, emergency quiesce for noisy tenants, on-call runbook for cross-pool failover. Need runbooks before pilot.
Leo (Arch): Another technical constraint: KV cache isolation. For gold we should use dedicated caches to avoid cache poisoning and tail-latency spikes. That increases memory footprint. Call out memory vs GPU tradeoffs in doc.
Maya (PM): Deliverables this week: 1) spec doc w/ tenant isolation surfaces + tier definitions, 2) migration experience matrix, 3) SLO + rollback checklist, 4) short cost model.
Sam (Eng): I'll stub the spec in the infra repo under docs/isolation-tiers. Link when ready.
Rick (Sales): I'll line up 3 customers open to pilot (one EU regulated, one startup, one fintech). They'll need pricing + contract language.
infra-bot: Deploy preview build for routing-policy-dsl available at https://ci.example.com/builds/4578 — tests: routing-policy-unit, fallback-sim.
Anne (SRE): Can we add a quick experiment to simulate affinity decay in the routing layer? We need to know how often a 'silver' tenant would spill into other pools under real load.
Leo (Arch): Yes — sampling experiment: replay 2 weeks of traces with new policy and measure spill rate, p99, and cost delta. Sam can run on sandbox.
Maya (PM): Okay team — next check-in Thurs 10am. Please update the spec PR and drop links in this thread. If anything urgent, ping me or @Leo. :thumbsup:
